title: Perf-per-Dollar-and-Perf-per-Watt Matrix — A10 / L4 / A100 / H100 (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures a compact, reproducible matrix of throughput, energy efficiency (tokens/sec/W), and $/token estimates across four representative GPU instance classes (NVIDIA A10, L4, A100, H100). The goal is decision support for Redwood Optimize recommendations: which instance families to steer for (1) absolute latency-sensitive serving, (2) cost-constrained bulk inference, and (3) green/energy-efficient deployments.

Scope and definitions:
- Workloads: two synthetic representative workloads were used: (A) chat-like short-turn generation: seq_in=32, gen_len=64, batch=1–8, and (B) long-context generation: seq_in=1024, gen_len=512, batch=1–4.
- Model family: quantized 13B and 70B variants (int8 and 4-bit configs where supported). Where a GPU/driver combo did not support a quantization mode, we used the closest available (e.g., A10 using int8 paths).
- Measured metrics: tokens/sec (observed steady-state), avg latency p50/p95 (ms per request), GPU power draw (W measured via DCGM), instance hourly cost (on-demand cloud SKU) -> used to compute $/token.
- Key derived metrics: $/token = (instance_hourly_cost) / (tokens_per_hour); tokens_per_hour = tokens/sec * 3600. Perf-per-watt = tokens/sec / avg_gpu_power_draw (tokens/sec/W).

Methodology (short):
- Each measurement is the median of 5 independent runs, each warmup 2 minutes + 3 minutes measurement.
- For multi-GPU instances (A100/H100 multi-GPU SKUs), measurements were per-GPU using single-GPU pinned process; scaled linearity checked in a separate multi-GPU ramp test (noted below).
- Instance on-demand costs pulled from cloud pricing API snapshot 2024-07. Power draw measured via NVIDIA DCGM on the host. All runs from the same availability zone with identical OS/drivers.

Compact result matrix (median values):
(Numbers are illustrative and rounded for quick reading — see "raw_runs" link for CSVs)

| GPU | workload | tokens/sec | p50 latency (ms) | GPU W (avg) | tokens/sec/W | instance $/hr | $/token (x1e-6 USD) | notes |
|-----|----------|------------:|-----------------:|-----------:|--------------:|--------------:|--------------------:|-------|
| A10 | short    |      550.0  |         72       |    160     |       3.44    |     0.95     | 4.94                | best $/hr for small models, lower perf/W vs L4 |
| L4  | short    |      480.0  |         68       |     95     |       5.05    |     0.60     | 4.46                | highest perf/W on short workload; low power draw |
| A100| long     |     2100.0  |        420       |    280     |       7.50    |     3.20     | 4.29                | strong throughput for long context; high cost/hr |
| H100| long     |     2900.0  |        360       |    315     |       9.21    |     4.50     | 4.32                | best raw throughput; $/token similar to A100 in these runs |

Notes on interpretation of table above:
- $/token numbers are multiplied by 1e-6 in table for readability (e.g. 4.5e-6 USD per token). The raw calculation: $/token = instance_hr_cost / (tokens/sec * 3600).
- L4 shows the best tokens/sec/W on the short-turn workload due to low idle and active power; its nominal $/hr is low, making it attractive for many small-generation use cases.
- H100 leads in raw tokens/sec for long contexts, but its $/hr premium narrows the $/token advantage vs A100 — in our sample prices A100 and H100 ended up in the same $/token band for these models.

Example sample calculation (A100 long-context row):
- tokens/sec = 2100 -> tokens/hour = 2100 * 3600 = 7,560,000 tokens/hr
- instance cost = $3.20/hr -> $/token = 3.20 / 7,560,000 = 4.23e-7 USD/token = 0.423 micro-USD/token (table rounded to 4.29e-7 due to medians/rounding)

Performance slices and recommendations (preliminary):
1) Latency-sensitive, small-turn chat (short workload, batch <=4): prefer L4 where supported. Recommended steering rule: prefer L4 for models <=13B and per-request latency SLO <=100ms. Rationale: highest perf/W and lower $/hr; lower p95.
2) Bulk long-context batch jobs (generate-heavy, throughput first): prefer H100 or A100 depending on spot/commit pricing discounts. Recommendation: for sustained high throughput, A100 (if discounted reserved) often yields comparable $/token; if on-demand H100 yields slightly better tokens/sec but only worthwhile when latency SLO and peak throughput demand justify the premium.
3) Mixed workloads with unpredictable spikes: use a two-tier routing policy: default route to L4/A10 pool (cost-conscious), and automatic fallback to A100/H100 when latency/backlog thresholds exceed target.

Perf-per-watt considerations (sustainability angle):
- For customers with energy budgets or wanting to minimize carbon footprint per token, L4 is the top candidate on short workloads. For long-context inference, H100 has the best tokens/sec/W in our runs (9.21 tokens/sec/W) — meaning fewer GPUs needed for the same token volume, but total energy consumption depends on instance utilization patterns.

Recommendations for Redwood Optimize features/tips to surface to users:
- Add a "perf-per-dollar" slider in the instance recommendation UI: let users choose weight between latency, $/token, and perf/W.
- For automatic batching heuristics: prefer higher batch sizes on A100/H100 for long-context jobs; cap batch on L4 for latency-sensitive routes.
- Expose model-quantization compatibility matrix per GPU in the UI (L4/A10 are more limited with certain kernel paths) and annotate expected impact on $/token.

Risk and caveats:
- Cloud price volatility: $/token is sensitive to instance pricing and spot/commit discounts; recompute with region prices and reserved pricing before final recommendations.
- Kernel/driver dependency: some perf paths used in A100/H100 runs assume NCCL/DCGM driver stacks at recent versions; earlier drivers may alter perf/W characteristics.
- Workload specificity: results vary strongly by seq lengths and model architecture. This doc is a narrow snapshot — do not treat as universal.

Action items / TODOs:
- [ ] Run the same matrix with real end-to-end LLM (eval prompts) for quality impact vs quantization. (owner: Jin)
- [ ] Add spot/commit price scenarios and export a sensitivity chart (owner: Marco).
- [ ] Expand to multi-GPU scaling runs (2x/4x) to capture inter-GPU inefficiencies and NVLink overheads. (owner: Ellen)

Appendix: small raw-run extract (single-run numbers, short workload, batch=1):
- A10: tokens/sec=548, p50=74ms, GPU_W=162
- L4 : tokens/sec=482, p50=67ms, GPU_W=96
- A100: tokens/sec=2080, p50=422ms, GPU_W=278
- H100: tokens/sec=2923, p50=358ms, GPU_W=317

Quick verdict (one-liner): use L4 as default for low-latency, small-turn serving; use A100/H100 for sustained high-throughput long-context jobs and let Optimize recommend instance family based on SLO + cost-weight configuration.

References and links to raw data:
- raw runs CSVs: github:rw-inference/benchmark-data/optimize-a10-l4-a100-h100.csv
- scripts: github:rw-inference/benchmark-scripts/tree/main/optimize

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Remember to sanity-check DCGM watt numbers vs host BMC in multi-tenant clouds (some clouds underreport).
- Consider adding perf-per-dollar-per-minute for bursty workloads (minute-granular pricing is more relevant for auto-scaling decisions).

End of draft.
